newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak group says seeks more trade with China.
newsitem.headline: Slovak group says seeks more trade with China.

text.p: Slovakia is seeking ways to increase mutual trade with China, mainly by widening the assortment of goods exported, Slovak Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SOPK) Chairman Peter Mihok said on Thursday.
"There is a big potential for Slovak products on the Chinese market, but we also need to diversify our exports," Mihok said after meeting with representatives CCPIT, the Chinese counterpart of SOPK.
Trade between Slovakia and China over the first seven months of the year totalled $73.3 million compared with $73 million for all of 1995.

Mihok said exports to China totalled $32.1 million, of which engineering and transport equipment accounted for 90 percent. Chinese exports to Slovakia totalled $41.2 million so far this year, comprising mostly textiles and clothing.
Mihok said tyres, chemical products, medical equipment and pharmaceuticals were prime candidates for exporting.
But, he said, a lack of pro-export programmes has hurt companies looking to sell their wares abroad.
"So far Slovakia's main disadvantage against other strong exporters has been the financial model of covering its exports to China," Mihok said, but did not elaborate.
Mihok said Slovakia should also focus more on creating joint-ventures with Chinese partners.
One such project is already underway between heavy engineering company ZTS TEES Martin and China's Wanan Guanming for assembling truck engines in the town of Jixi in the eastern province of Anhui.
